segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Eh, still a bit tired one lah, but okay. Got some pain here, you know.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Can you tell me more about the pain? Where is it, and how bad is it on a scale of 1 to 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Mostly around the tummy area, like where they cut. Maybe 4 or 5? Not too bad, but there.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or vomiting since waking up? You mentioned before you have GERD, so we’re keeping an eye on that.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yeah, a bit of nausea earlier, but not throwing up. My throat also sore, like something stuck there.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: The sore throat is probably from the tube we used during surgery. It should get better in a day or two. Breathing okay otherwise?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing fine, just the throat pain. But I don’t remember anything about the surgery, very foggy one.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That’s normal because of the anesthesia. We’ll monitor your blood pressure and sugars given your hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Any dizziness or shortness of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No dizziness, but moving around a bit uncomfortable because of the belly. BMI 32 also, so maybe harder to move?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: We’ll get physio to help with mobility. For your GERD, avoid lying flat and take your meds as prescribed. Any other concerns?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, think that’s all. Thanks for checking on me.
